changelog.entry: Two more chapters and the periodic table. Burning (methane, propane, ethanol, pentane, ethyne, sulfur, sugar and ammonia) and Oxides and Salts (limestone, slaked lime, limewater, baking soda, peroxide, antacid, rust and fertiliser) add 16 orders, 24 in all. From chapter 2 you choose what comes out from four lists before the dials open: only one can be balanced, and a wrong choice just says why. Chapter 3 draws bracket groups such as (OH). Each new element you use lights a tile on the periodic table, and its card says what it is for. Five shelved orders open the next chapter.

The bench is playable: eight orders in Bench Basics, a flask for everything that goes in and comes out, a dial in front of each, and an atom ledger that counts every element on both sides and says how many too many or too few. Run puts the compound on the shelf. Nothing is timed and nothing can go wrong.
